clue.text: Sport fans cool off in queue at gate?

indicators.note: something taken off is removed, so the matching letters come away from the longer word

blocks.note: taken as written
to fan something is to cool it with moving air
the airport announcement that sends passengers to queue at the departure gate

explanation.surface: Sports supporters stuck waiting at a stadium gate, trying to cool down.
explanation.walkthrough: Take FAN (to cool) away from FANS and only S is left; add NOW BOARDING, the call heard at an airport gate, to get SNOWBOARDING.
explanation.definitionFit: Snowboarding is a winter pastime practised on a single board down slopes, so it is one example of a sport.

clue.text: Reserved rowing boat?

blocks.note: a four is a racing boat rowed by four oarsmen; the answer's first word says to voice it

explanation.surface: Someone has booked a rowing boat ahead of time.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: the answer itself is the instruction. Take a 'four', a rowing boat, and say it, and you have SPOKEN FOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Something spoken for has already been claimed or booked by another person, which is what reserved means.

clue.text: Second item is too much for gossip

indicators.note: the words given are longer than needed, so only a stretch inside them is kept

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A second piece of news is one item more than a gossip column can take.
explanation.walkthrough: secOND ITem holds the answer; 'is too much for' says the two words contain more letters than ON-DIT needs.
explanation.definitionFit: On-dit is French borrowed into English for a piece of hearsay, literally 'it is said', so it means a rumour or gossip.

clue.text: Out of line, belays orders on a ship

indicators.note: when one thing is out of another it has gone from it, so a letter is taken away
to order things is to arrange them, so the remaining letters are put into a new sequence

blocks.note: L is the standard abbreviation for line
taken as written

explanation.surface: Off the rope, a sailor makes fast lines with belaying orders aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Belay' is a nautical word for securing a rope, which keeps the eye on the ship; drop L from BELAYS and rearrange BEAYS.
explanation.definitionFit: Travelling by sea means going over water aboard a vessel, so it matches being on a ship.

clue.text: Spirited maiden soon captivates legendary hero

indicators.note: to captivate is to take captive, so one piece holds the others inside it

blocks.note: someone game is plucky and willing
M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over
anon is an old literary word for soon

explanation.surface: A lively young woman is soon charmed by a hero of legend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maiden' suggests a girl, but in crosswords it often means a cricket over with no runs scored. Anon is an archaic word for soon.
explanation.definitionFit: Agamemnon was the Greek king who led the army against Troy in Homer's epic, a figure of myth and legend.

clue.text: Person who inspires African country after sticking notice up

indicators.note: things stuck into something end up inside it, so pieces go within another
in a down clue, going up means reading from the bottom, so the order is turned round

blocks.note: an ad is an advertisement or notice
Mali is a country in West Africa
à la means after the manner of, as in à la mode

explanation.surface: A notice posted up about an African nation shows someone who motivates it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' looks like a time word but means 'in the style of', from French à la. In a down clue 'up' sends the whole thing upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tibetan spiritual leader is widely admired as a source of inspiration and moral guidance worldwide.

clue.text: One’s heading into harbour for University of Scandinavia

indicators.note: a heading sits at the top, so only the opening letter of the word is used
going into a word for something else means taking its place there

blocks.note: to nurse a grudge is to harbour it
U is the abbreviation for university
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone heads into a port to study at a Scandinavian university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harbour' looks like a port but is a verb, as in harbour a grudge, NURSE; O replaces its U.
explanation.definitionFit: Norse is the adjective for things relating to ancient or medieval Scandinavia, its people and language.

clue.text: Leaving with it, bandit has not entirely gone straight, sadly this?

definitions.text: Leaving with it, bandit has not entirely gone straight, sadly this?

indicators.note: words that are leaving go away, so their letters are dropped from the next word
only part of the word is wanted, so its last letter goes
something that ends sadly has turned out badly, so the letters are jumbled into disorder

blocks.note: and means together with
taken as written
taken as written
the word without its final letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A robber who was going straight is caught making off with the loot again.
explanation.walkthrough: AND and IT leave BANDIT, leaving B; then GON plus STRAIGHT is rearranged. Read whole, the clue describes the thief caught red-handed.
explanation.definitionFit: Bang to rights is British slang for being caught red-handed with clear proof of guilt, exactly the robber's fate.

clue.text: Given permission to speak in a normal voice

indicators.note: speaking means saying words, so it is their sound that matters, not spelling

blocks.note: someone given permission has been allowed

explanation.surface: Someone is finally allowed to speak up in an ordinary voice.
explanation.walkthrough: ALLOWED and ALOUD sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Reading aloud means voicing words audibly rather than silently or whispering, so in a normal speaking voice.

clue.text: Text covers the majority of duck shooters

indicators.note: a cover goes round something, so one piece wraps the other
a majority is most but not all, so the end is lost

blocks.note: SMS is the abbreviation for a text message
the mallard is the commonest wild duck

explanation.surface: A message describes most of the people who shoot ducks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shooters' seems to be the hunters of the surface, but it means guns.
explanation.definitionFit: Small arms are handguns and rifles, and 'shooter' is informal slang for a gun.

clue.text: Extra flexible in one’s thinking?

blocks.note: supple means bending easily
mental means relating to the mind

explanation.surface: Someone is unusually open-minded.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one phrase about an open mind, but it splits into a word for the body and one for the mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Supplemental means added on top of what is already there, an additional or further amount.

clue.text: Rearranging date? Reagan hasn’t a Scooby-Doo?

indicators.note: rearranging means putting in a different order, so the letters are mixed up
what something hasn't got is missing, so one letter is dropped

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A diary clash, with Reagan's aide asked whether he has a clue.
explanation.walkthrough: One A comes out of DATE REAGAN, then the rest is mixed. 'Hasn't a Scooby-Doo' plays on rhyming slang: not a Scooby (Doo) means not a clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Scooby-Doo, the cartoon dog who solves mysteries, is a Great Dane, so he is an example of the breed.

clue.text: Universal plugging elaborate epic set in winter

indicators.note: a plug fills a hole, so one piece is pushed inside another
to elaborate is to work something out in more detail, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: U is the film certificate for Universal
taken as written

explanation.surface: A universal tale fills out a sweeping epic story set during winter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set in winter' sounds like a film's setting, but 'set' is a verb: to harden. U goes into ICEP, a rearranged EPIC.
explanation.definitionFit: To ice up is to become coated or frozen with ice, which is how water sets solid in cold weather.

clue.text: When little activity is observed from fluorine salt?

blocks.note: of can mean from, as in a man of Kent
F is the chemical symbol for fluorine
to salt food is to season it

explanation.surface: A chemist notes that little reacts when fluorine salt is involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salt' looks like a noun after the chemical, but it is a verb meaning to season.
explanation.definitionFit: The off-season is the quiet period of the year when a business, resort or sport has little going on.

clue.text: European boy band doing a turn in Elgar show

indicators.note: turning round faces the other way, so the letters run backwards
one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for European
a lad is a boy
R.E.M. is an American rock band
Elgar is the setter of this puzzle, so he refers to himself as me

explanation.surface: A European boy band performs a turn in a show by the composer Elgar.
explanation.walkthrough: Elgar is the composer and also this puzzle's setter, so he means ME. Emmerdale is a long-running British TV soap opera set in the Yorkshire Dales.
explanation.definitionFit: Emmerdale is a British television serial drama, so it is a programme or show on TV.

clue.text: Now one’s concerned with matter after overturning car

indicators.note: something overturned is upside down, and in a down clue that reads bottom to top

blocks.note: in means fashionable, of the moment
one is I, and I's is I am, written IM
re means about or concerning
pus is the yellow matter in an infected wound

explanation.surface: After a car crash, someone is suddenly a student of physical matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Matter' looks like a physics word but is the medical sense, PUS. IN, IM, RE and PUS read upwards give SUPERMINI.
explanation.definitionFit: A supermini is a small hatchback, the category of compact car between city cars and family saloons.

clue.text: Big tech concern almost inspiring a shock

indicators.note: almost all of the word is used, so the final letter is cut
to inspire is literally to breathe in, so one piece is taken inside another

blocks.note: Apple is a giant technology company
taken as written

explanation.surface: A huge technology firm almost gives everyone a fright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inspiring' reads as encouraging, but here it is literal: breathing in, so taking a letter inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To appal someone is to fill them with horror or dismay, a verb synonym for shock.

clue.text: Seemingly good casino game cancels ball’s last spin

indicators.note: the final letter of the word is the one to use
cancelled things are struck out, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: pi is slang for pious, ostentatiously virtuous
roulette is the wheel-and-ball casino game
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A roulette wheel stops the ball's final spin, deceptively good for the player.
explanation.walkthrough: PI is crossword slang for pious, which is only seemingly good. ROULETTE loses the L.
explanation.definitionFit: A pirouette is a ballet dancer's rapid turn on one foot, so it is a kind of spin.

clue.text: 60 mins before noon? This is possibly sacred

blocks.note: sixty minutes is one hour, written 1 HR with the 1 as I
a.m. stands for ante meridiem, before midday

explanation.surface: An hour before midday is presented as a holy time.
explanation.walkthrough: The digit 1 stands in for the letter I. The definition is vague on purpose, since the answer is an obscure religious word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ihram is the plain white garment, and the state of consecration, of Muslim pilgrims to Mecca, so it is held sacred.

clue.text: Label, astral sign, associated with Lovecraft, say?

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing for a noun

blocks.note: to pen a tag is to write a label
the Ram is Aries, a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A star sign label linked with the horror writer H. P. Lovecraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Astral sign' seems to describe the answer, a five-pointed star, but it is Aries, the RAM.
explanation.definitionFit: The five-pointed star figure is an occult symbol that recurs in H. P. Lovecraft's horror fiction.

clue.text: Fired up promoter

blocks.note: first meaning: overexcited, highly strung
second meaning: someone who publicises something loudly

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as an enthusiastic promoter; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyper is informal for overexcited, and a hyper is also one who hypes, drumming up publicity.

clue.text: Flat with scratched floor, this must have gone wrong!

indicators.note: in a down clue the floor is the bottom, and scratching it out removes the lowest letter

blocks.note: lying in one flat plane

explanation.surface: A flat with a scratched floor shows that something went badly wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: PLANAR loses its R. The definition is a wry one: if you are now on the backup scheme, the original must have failed.
explanation.definitionFit: Plan A is the first intended course of action; falling back on Plan B implies it went wrong.

clue.text: Could it be Labour-antagonistic choice of shift?

definitions.text: Could it be Labour-antagonistic choice of shift?

blocks.note: surface reading: a worker who resents labour picking which shift to work
setter's reading: someone against the Labour Party, on the left, would swing the other way politically

explanation.surface: A worker who hates labour chooses which shift to take.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour is the British left-wing party; opposing it, you shift direction to the political opposite of left.
explanation.definitionFit: A swing towards conservative politics is called a turn to the right, the opposite of the left-wing Labour stance.

clue.text: England’s rebel captain dealing with lies on board longboat

indicators.note: whatever lies on board a vessel is inside it, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: a gig is a long light rowing boat
re means concerning or dealing with

explanation.surface: An English rebel captain reckons with deceit aboard a Viking ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Tony Greig lost the England cricket captaincy in 1977 for recruiting players to Kerry Packer's breakaway World Series Cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Tony Greig captained England's cricket team and became a rebel by signing up to Packer's rival series.

clue.text: Body? Leader of investigation misses it in ball park

indicators.note: a leader goes in front, so only the opening letter is wanted
what is missed is absent, so that letter drops out

blocks.note: the first letter of the word
taken as written
or so means approximately, a ballpark figure

explanation.surface: The head detective fails to spot a body lying in a baseball stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Body' and 'investigation' set up a murder scene, but the answer is anatomy. IT without I leaves T.
explanation.definitionFit: The torso is the trunk of the human body, without head or limbs, so 'body' with a query fits.

clue.text: Cook rationalises squeezing out oil pods

indicators.note: squeezing something out forces it away, so those letters are removed
to cook the books is to falsify them, so the letters are doctored into a new form

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A chef cuts back on oil when preparing seed pods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' sits at the front looking like the subject, but it is the anagram signal; remove O, I and L from RATIONALISES.
explanation.definitionFit: Star anise is a spice made from the dried star-shaped seed pods of an evergreen Chinese tree.

clue.text: Back one in line dispensing with western networks

indicators.note: going back means travelling the opposite way, so the letters run in reverse
dispensing with something is doing without it, so it is dropped

blocks.note: a waiter is someone waiting in a queue
W is the abbreviation for western

explanation.surface: Western computer networks are dropped from a queue, sending one back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One in line' is someone who waits, a WAITER, not a restaurant server. Retia is the plural of rete, an anatomy term.
explanation.definitionFit: A rete is an anatomical network of blood vessels or nerves, and retia is its plural.

clue.text: Took call in full pub

indicators.note: one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: whole means complete or full
to take food is to eat it
to ring someone is to call them on the phone

explanation.surface: Someone answered the phone in a packed bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Took' looks like taking a call, but it stands alone as consumed food.
explanation.definitionFit: Watering hole is a jocular idiom for a pub or bar, borrowed from the pools where animals gather to drink.
